_comment: Written before deployment. Committed so the charges this week accepted are public.
THIS IS THE FIRST WEEK SINCE 11 WITH REAL PER-HOUR COMPUTE, and the first
where the headline feature is the expensive one. Zone-redundant HA is not a
checkbox: the Burstable tier does not support HA at all, so HA forces
General Purpose, and HA then doubles that compute.
CORRECTED 2026-11-22: an earlier version of this file claimed a $1,883/hour
meter. That was a 3-year reservation term total misread as an hourly rate by
price_check.py. Jay questioned the number; it did not survive the check.

acknowledged.vCore: NOT REACHED. 32 tiers, dearest 76.979/hr -- a ~96-vCore Memory Optimized server, about $1,847/day. Real and reachable if the wrong SKU is picked, which is why the server's sku_name is pinned in Terraform. CORRECTED 2026-11-22: this previously read 1,883.00/hr. That figure was a THREE-YEAR RESERVATION TOTAL that price_check.py was reading as an hourly rate -- the same SKU's consumption rate is 0.1791/hr. The tool now excludes type=Reservation rows; 28 were being counted here.

the_tier_decision.burstable_b1ms: 0.0204/hr. Cheapest, and REJECTED: the Burstable tier supports no form of high availability, zone-redundant or same-zone. Choosing it would mean dropping HA from the week's claim.
the_tier_decision.general_purpose_2_vcore_with_zone_redund: 0.4104/hr -- HA doubles compute because it runs a standby. CHOSEN.
the_tier_decision.why: A configured HA setting proves nothing. The week's claim is a failover actually performed with the downtime measured, and that is only possible on a tier that supports HA.

predicted_cost._comment: Stated BEFORE deployment so the invoice can contradict it.
predicted_cost.bound: a TIME window, not a daily cap -- this meter bills per hour and cannot be capped like ingestion
predicted_cost.storage: 32 GB minimum, ~0.115/GB/month, prorated -- pennies for a 3 hour window
predicted_cost.backup_storage: 0.114 per GB/month, free up to the provisioned storage size
predicted_cost.if_left_running_24h: 9.85 compute alone -- more than week 11's entire 7.19 invoice
predicted_cost.discipline: deploy, validate, fail over, measure, destroy in one sitting. There is no cap that saves this one; only teardown does.

residual_risks: A per-hour meter has no equivalent of week 13's daily_quota_gb. The only bound is destroying it, so cleanup.sh runs the same day and the figure plan has no slot that requires the server to survive overnight.
A failed teardown here costs ~$10/day rather than ~$0, so cleanup verification asserts the server is gone against Azure rather than trusting the destroy exit code.
Storage is billed from creation to deletion and is not prorated by usage, so an idle server still charges for its disk.
